children: By Kentaro Matsumoto / Yomiuri Shimbun Staff Writer

Japan's financial watchdog will monitor the impact of rising long-term interest rates on financial institutions, such as the widening of unrealized losses on government bonds, the head of the organization said in a recent interview with The Yomiuri Shimbun.

"We want to thoroughly grasp the status of assets and, if there are any financial institutions that are not taking appropriate action, quickly discover them and take action (as the agency)," said Yutaka Ito, commissioner of the Financial Services Agency.

The yield on Japan's long-term government bond reached 3% on Sept. 1 for the first time in 30 years, driven by factors including concerns over the government's fiscal health and speculation that the Bank of Japan may accelerate interest rate hikes. As yields on government bonds rise, their prices fall, causing the valuation losses on such bonds held by financial institutions to swell and weigh on their operations.

Ito emphasized, "Even if losses are occurring, the question is whether this is a dangerous sign or not, and if we cannot determine from the data alone, we will conduct hearings or inspections." On the other hand, he also noted that rising interest rates "present a major opportunity" for the financial services sector. "I want them to focus on increasing returns while properly managing risks," he added.

He also touched on the use of artificial intelligence, saying: "We are collecting a lot of data, so we will use AI to analyze it. We will also streamline internal administrative tasks using AI, and if that frees up time, we can redirect staff to areas where we are short-staffed, such as inspectors."
